ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a schematic diagram of port distribution, marked with port points such as a, b, c, and d, and with lines of latitude and longitude as position references. Port a is located in the northern part of the figure, and its position is obviously farther north than ports such as b, c, and d, close to around 50°N. Reasoning: The question asks the main factor causing the thawing date of Port a to be later than that of the other ports. The timing of port thawing is mainly affected by temperature; the higher the latitude, the less solar radiation received, the lower the temperature, the longer the freezing period, and therefore the later the thawing date. Since Port a has the highest latitude in the figure, the main factor causing its later thawing date is latitude.

method.method_draft: 先描述图像：图中有多个港口点，a港口位于图幅北部，位置比b、c、d更偏北，并接近或高于50°N附近。再读题：题目问a港口解冻日期比其他港口晚的主要因素。将图上港口纬度差异与气温规律连接：纬度越高，气温越低，冰冻期越长，解冻越晚。因此主要因素是纬度。
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中为一幅港口分布示意图，标有a、b、c、d等港口点，并有纬线和经线作为位置参照。a港口位于图幅北部，位置明显比b、c、d等港口更偏北，接近50°N附近。推理：题目问a港口解冻日期比其他港口晚的主要因素。港口解冻早晚主要受气温影响；纬度越高，获得的太阳辐射越少，气温越低，冰冻期越长，因而解冻日期越晚。由于图中a港口纬度最高，所以导致其解冻日期较晚的主要因素是纬度。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct map-coordinate route: it relies on reading the relative position of port a against the latitude graticule and comparing it with the other marked ports. This is the most straightforward route to the answer.
planner_metadata.image_role: Inspect the map first: locate the black-dot ports a, b, c, and d; note the latitude reference marked 50°N and the positions of the ports relative to it. Port a is drawn farther north than b, c, and d.
planner_metadata.text_role: Read the question wording: it asks for the main factor causing port a to thaw later than the other ports, not for the exact date or the port name.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the geographic rule that, in the Northern Hemisphere, higher latitude generally receives less solar radiation and has lower temperatures, so sea/harbor ice melts later in spring.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Weakly distinct diagnostic route: instead of starting from the coordinate line alone, it treats the map as a regional port distribution map and evaluates possible controlling factors by comparing the shared coastal/near-water setting of the ports, then isolates the systematic north–south difference. Because the problem is essentially single-cause, this is only weakly distinct from the direct latitude comparison.
planner_metadata.image_role: Inspect the spatial pattern on the map: all labeled points are ports around the North American water bodies, but a is the only one placed in the far northern part of the distribution, while c and d are farther south/east and b is also lower in latitude.
planner_metadata.text_role: Read the prompt as asking for a '主要因素', so use the map-visible dominant geographic difference among the ports rather than inventing unavailable data such as exact ocean currents or local depth.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the climate-control principle for port freezing: among ports in the same broad temperate-cold region, spring thaw timing is controlled mainly by heat conditions; the most stable map-visible proxy for heat is latitude. Higher-latitude ports remain colder longer and thaw later.
